title: "Log Existing Code in One Call"
description: "Capture messages, warnings, and errors without editing a function, then add call information when you need to debug."
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Log Existing Code in One Call}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
old_options <- options(width = 90L)
saved_logfile <- loggit2::get_logfile()
saved_level <- loggit2::set_log_level("DEBUG", confirm = FALSE)
saved_echo <- loggit2::set_echo(FALSE, confirm = FALSE)
saved_calls <- loggit2::set_call_options(confirm = FALSE)
```

You already have a function or script that emits messages, warnings or errors.
To record those conditions, wrap the call you already make:

```{r one-call, eval = FALSE}
loggit2::with_loggit(your_function())
```

No changes inside the function are needed. The default log is in R's temporary
directory; no logger object or configuration file is required.

## Try it with an unchanged function

Here is a small stand-in for code from an existing script or another package:

```{r existing-function}
import_data <- function() {
  base::message("Reading input")
  base::warning("One row has an empty value")
  120L
}
```

Choose a separate file for this tutorial, then wrap the function call:

```{r capture}
logfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".ndjson")
rows <- loggit2::with_loggit(import_data(), logfile = logfile, echo = FALSE)
rows
loggit2::read_logs(logfile)[c("log_lvl", "log_msg")]
```

The function still returns `120L`. The message and warning are still displayed,
and both appear in the log. The optional `logfile` argument picks the destination;
`echo = FALSE` removes the extra JSON output to stdout.

`with_loggit()` records signaled R conditions, not ordinary `print()` or `cat()`
output. It also does not capture conditions already handled inside the expression.

## Handle errors without losing the log

Put recovery logic outside `with_loggit()` so that the error reaches its logging
handler before the outer `tryCatch()` handles it:

```{r recover}
read_input <- function() base::stop("Input file is missing")

result <- tryCatch(
  loggit2::with_loggit(read_input(), logfile = logfile, echo = FALSE),
  error = function(e) "Use a fallback input"
)
result
tail(loggit2::read_logs(logfile)[c("log_lvl", "log_msg")], 1L)
```

Without the outer `tryCatch()`, the error stops execution as usual. Conversely,
if `read_input()` catches the error internally, an outer `with_loggit()` cannot
record the condition that has already been handled.

The same ordering matters when silencing output. Keep the suppression outside
the capture if you still want the condition in the log:

```{r quiet-capture}
suppressMessages(
  loggit2::with_loggit(base::message("A quiet progress update"),
                       logfile = logfile, echo = FALSE)
)
```

The message is now logged without being displayed. `echo = FALSE` alone would
only remove the additional JSON output.

## Capture only the detail you need

For a noisy section, set the capture level on that call:

```{r capture-level}
loggit2::with_loggit({
  base::message("Progress update: displayed but not logged")
}, logfile = logfile, log_level = "ERROR", echo = FALSE)
```

The session's log level is unchanged. These arguments configure the handlers in
`with_loggit()`; they do not reconfigure a direct `loggit()` or condition wrapper
inside the expression. See [configuration and scope](further_configurations.html).

## Avoid recording the same condition twice

Choose either a `loggit2` condition wrapper or `with_loggit()` for a given
condition. For example, this combination can produce two entries:

```{r double-logging, eval = FALSE}
loggit2::with_loggit(loggit2::warning("Incomplete input"))
```

Instead, capture an unchanged `base::warning()` call, or use
`loggit2::warning()` directly. Nested `with_loggit()` calls can likewise record
the same condition more than once.

## Find the origin of an event

When you need more detail, enable call logging. The condition wrappers and
`debuginfo()` use the session log file, so select it for this section:

```{r enable-calls}
previous_logfile <- loggit2::set_logfile(logfile, confirm = FALSE)
previous_calls <- loggit2::set_call_options(
  log_call = TRUE, full_stack = FALSE, confirm = FALSE
)

inspect_input <- function() {
  loggit2::debuginfo("Inspecting the input header", echo = FALSE)
}
run_import <- function() inspect_input()

run_import()
tail(loggit2::read_logs(logfile)[c("log_lvl", "log_msg", "log_call")], 1L)
```

`debuginfo()` writes a DEBUG entry without signaling a condition. Unlike a plain
`loggit("DEBUG", ...)` event, it can record the calling function. It is filtered
out when the session level is below DEBUG, unless `.loggit = TRUE` is supplied.

To see how the call was reached, enable the full stack and run the same code:

```{r full-stack}
loggit2::set_call_options(log_call = TRUE, full_stack = TRUE, confirm = FALSE)
run_import()

last_call <- tail(loggit2::read_logs(logfile)$log_call, 1L)
cat(tail(strsplit(last_call, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]], 2L), sep = "\n")
```

Only the last two stack lines are shown here. Stack details depend on the
execution environment and the available source information. A condition object
created earlier cannot generally reconstruct its original full stack. Direct
`loggit()` events do not infer a condition call: their `log_call` field is `NA`.

Restore the previous session settings when you are done:

```{r restore-calls}
loggit2::set_call_options(.arg_list = previous_calls, confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::set_logfile(previous_logfile, confirm = FALSE, create = FALSE)
```

For run IDs, filenames and other context fields, use explicit events as shown in
[Analyze Logs from a Data Pipeline](structured-logs.html). Return to
[Getting Started](loggit2.html) for an overview of all three logging approaches.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
loggit2::set_logfile(saved_logfile, confirm = FALSE, create = FALSE)
loggit2::set_log_level(saved_level, confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::set_echo(saved_echo, confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::set_call_options(.arg_list = saved_calls, confirm = FALSE)
options(old_options)
unlink(logfile)
```
